subject: Next steps: Carelyft security questionnaire & log/backup retention
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ortiz <elena.ortiz@carelyft.com>, Michael Tan <michael.tan@carelyft.com>
Cc: Carelyft Procurement <procurement@carelyft.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-07-31T17:12:00Z
Subject: Follow-up & questionnaire (backup/log retention)

Hi Elena / Michael —

Thanks again for the time today — appreciate the clear background on Carelyft’s use case and the importance of strict retention/deletion controls for PHI. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

- Recap: Carelyft is evaluating Redwood Hosted API for inferencing PHI in a production workflow. Key asks from today: SOC 2 scope, GDPR/HIPAA deletion guarantees, log retention windows (access logs / request logs / KV cache traces), and backup retention + encryption.
- Attachments: I’ve attached our redacted SOC 2 Type II (Q2 2027) and a short backup-retention summary. I’m also attaching our vendor security questionnaire to expedite any procurement/security review on your side.

Action items / asks for you:
1) Please confirm required retention windows for: a) request logs, b) aggregated logs, c) backups (full snapshots). Example options you mentioned on the call: 6 months vs 7 years — we can support both but wanted to confirm which baseline you need.
2) Are there any regulatory hold requirements (legal holds) that would prevent deletion for subsets of data?
3) Please complete the attached questionnaire and indicate a preferred time for a technical follow-up (I’ve cc’d Vivek who can join for deeper infra questions).

Next steps we’ll take:
- Neha will provide a short note describing our deletion workflow and timeline for hosted vs private deployments.
- Vivek will prep answers on backup encryption, immutable backup support, and log export options.

If you prefer, we can block 30 minutes next week — here’s a scheduling link: https://calendly.com/redwood-sec/30min

Thanks,

Rachel Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0198
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Follow-up & questionnaire (backup/log retention)

Hi Rachel —

Thanks for the recap and for sending the docs. A few clarifying items so we can route this correctly to our InfoSec and legal teams: 

- Retention windows: For PHI-backed logs we typically require a 7-year retention for audit artifacts, but for request traces we may only need 12 months. I’ll confirm exact buckets with Legal tomorrow.
- Deletion: We have two constraints — (1) timely deletion of user-subject data on request (we expect vendor to remove customer-identifying content within a defined SLA), and (2) the ability to place data on legal hold which may extend retention for certain records.

Before we finalize: could you explicitly confirm whether your SOC 2 Type II covers backups and the process for removing data from backups? Does Redwood run immutable backups (WORM) or are backups deletable by policy? Also: how are backups encrypted (customer-managed keys vs Redwood-managed)?

We’ll start the questionnaire on our side but would like the sections you’ve highlighted answered (retention/deletion, backups/encryption, log export formats). Target for returning the completed questionnaire is EOD 2027-08-06 if possible.

Thanks,
Elena Ortiz
Head of Security Programs, Carelyft Health
elena.ortiz@carelyft.com

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ortiz <elena.ortiz@carelyft.com>, Michael Tan <michael.tan@carelyft.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-02T16:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Follow-up & questionnaire (backup/log retention)

Hi Elena —

Appreciate the quick reply and the timeframe. A few direct answers to the technical questions you raised, plus what we can offer as standard/defaults vs configurable options: 

1) SOC 2 scope: Our SOC 2 Type II report covers the control environment for the hosted Redwood API, including operational controls applied to backups and key management used by Redwood-operated storage. The redacted report shows control descriptions — we can provide a full SOC 2 package under an NDA if required.

2) Backups and deletion:
   - Default: Hosted backups are encrypted at rest using AES-256 with Redwood-managed keys. Backups are retained for 90 days by default.
   - Deletion: For routine deletion requests we remove customer data from live storage within 30 days. Backups are treated as recoverable snapshots and are marked for purge; typical purge completes within the 90-day backup retention window. For stricter deletion guarantees (e.g., within 7 days even for backups) we recommend a Dedicated or Private deployment where we can implement shorter immutable retention and customer-managed keying.
   - Immutable backups (WORM): We support write-once retention configurations for Dedicated/Private customers on request — this is not standard for self-serve hosted tenants.

3) Encryption / key management:
   - Hosted: Redwood-managed KMS (AES-256).
   - Dedicated/Private: Option for customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) and bring-your-own-key for storage encryption.

4) Logs and exports:
   - Default log retention: 30 days for request logs and operational traces on Hosted.
   - Extended retention: We can export logs to your S3 or SIEM (Splunk/Datadog) for long-term archival; we also offer per-customer extended retention plans up to multi-year.
   - Log format: JSON lines, request_id, timestamp, model, prompt_hash (no PII by default unless you send PHI in payloads — please let us know if you use tokenization/PII redaction).

5) Legal hold / litigation: We can implement hold flags at the account level to prevent deletion while preserving recoverability; this will affect backup purge timelines and may extend retention as required.

Attached: short backup-retention-summary.md and the vendor questionnaire with a few pre-filled fields to help speed your review.

Happy to hop on a 30-minute technical call — Rachel’s calendly is here: https://calendly.com/redwood-sec/30min. If it helps, I can loop in our CISO (Neha) for policy-level signoff.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
